drafts.title: Service requests — baseline table
drafts.prompt: Brooklyn 311 service-request list for a borough desk: shadcn data table with every field, status tabs, search, bulk assign.
drafts.scenario: typical + 15 missing resolutions + 2 missing streets + 700-char resolution

drafts.title: A · Triage queue grouped by severity
drafts.prompt: Replace the table with a queue: groups by severity (entire-building heat first), duplicates folded under one row, two-line list rows with wait time and status, closed requests behind a link.
drafts.scenario: typical + 15 missing resolutions + 2 missing streets + 700-char resolution
drafts.hypothesis: Grouping by severity makes the next request to act on the first row, without sorting or reading.
drafts.favors: picking the next request; phone use, because the same list works at 390
drafts.sacrifices: density (about 9 requests above the fold at 1440×900, against about 15 in B) and ad-hoc sorting or comparing by column

drafts.title: B · Focused table with detail rail
drafts.prompt: Keep a table for experts but cut it to six columns sorted by priority (P1–P3), wait time first, duplicates badged and sunk to the bottom, a Needs action default tab, and a fixed detail rail with the full agency note and actions. List rows below md.
drafts.scenario: typical + 15 missing resolutions + 2 missing streets + 700-char resolution; the 700-char note is on a closed row, so the default view does not show it
drafts.hypothesis: Experts keep scanning a table; showing the selected request's full note beside it removes the need to open rows.
drafts.favors: high-volume scanning and comparing rows; acting without leaving the list
drafts.sacrifices: 384px of width for the rail; priority is a computed code (P1–P3) the operator must learn and trust; duplicates still take rows
